transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message: Hello, this is calling from our company. Is this a good time to talk about your account?

transcript.speaker: user
transcript.message:
*sounding exhausted and slightly panicked* 

Oh... uh, I guess? I'm at work right now, on my break. Look, I know you're calling about the bill, and I'm so sorry, I just... I can't talk about this for long. My wife's in the hospital again and I'm barely holding it together. I want to pay, I really do, but right now... I just don't see how.

transcript.speaker: agent
transcript.message:
Thank you for being honest with me—I know this isn’t easy. I'm really sorry to hear your wife’s in the hospital again. That’s incredibly tough, and I want you to know I’m not here to add stress. My job is to help find a path forward that makes sense for your situation.

You said you *want* to pay, and that matters. It tells me you’re responsible and care about resolving this. So let’s keep that intention alive, but in a way that doesn’t overwhelm you right now.

Since you’re at work and short on time, I’ll keep this simple:  
Would it help if we paused any immediate payment expectations for now—say, for the next 30 to 60 days—so you can focus on your wife and your family? We can set up what we call a *hardship arrangement*, which means no collection activity, no fees added, and we’ll wait until things stabilize before starting payments.

Then, when you’re ready, we come back and set up something manageable—maybe $50 or $75 a month, whatever works. Does that sound like something that would give you the breathing room you need?

I just need a quick yes or no to move forward with the pause. And again, I’m truly sorry you’re going through this. We’ll take care of the rest when the time’s right.
